text:
Morgan Rielly returned to the Maple Leafs' lineup Tuesday in Chicago after missing time, and Toronto needs him. The team has lost nine of its last ten, and Rielly, in his 14th season and 970th game as a Leaf, is still the defenseman who runs its offense from the back.

His line is odd: 12 assists and zero goals in 19 games. Eight of those assists came in his last ten. The zero won't last; his chances add up to 1.52 expected goals, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net more than 99% of NHL defensemen last season. A scoring rate of 2.0 points per 60 is well above what our talent range expects, so the assists may slow even as the goals arrive.

The cost has always been defense. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting more chances with him on the ice last season than with almost any defenseman (bottom 5%). This year Toronto gets 48% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him, slightly better than without him. On a team searching for answers, he's still part of the solution.
headline: Rielly is back, still waiting on a goal
